title: How Does a Genome Produce an Organism?
problem: Investigate a foundational unsolved problem in biology: given the genome of a fertilized egg and the initial cellular and environmental conditions, can we predict the development of a functioning organism, including cell fates, spatial organization, body plan, and morphological variation? Genetic information is necessary but not a complete specification of developmental dynamics: maternal contributions, gene regulation, signaling, mechanics, stochasticity, and environment interact over time. Seek a mechanistic, quantitatively predictive theory rather than a descriptive catalog of developmental genes. Compare explanations and models in tractable model organisms, design falsifiable perturbations, and distinguish experimentally observed outcomes from simulated predictions. Avoid claiming that a single model system or cell lineage resolves the overarching question. Deliver bounded research hypotheses, causal tests, predictive benchmarks, uncertainty assessments, and failure criteria.

strategies.title: From gene regulation to cell fate
strategies.approach: For a defined early embryonic lineage, test whether measured gene-regulatory networks and initial states predict cell-fate decisions under unseen perturbations. Distinguish network sufficiency from post hoc fitting.
strategies.summary: A prospective cell-fate prediction benchmark with explicit errors.

strategies.title: How positional information becomes anatomy
strategies.approach: Compare morphogen-gradient, reaction-diffusion, and cell-interaction models for a specific spatial pattern. Specify measurements and perturbations that discriminate between models.
strategies.summary: A spatial pattern prediction and a decisive perturbation.

strategies.title: Cell mechanics and morphogenesis
strategies.approach: Assess how forces, adhesion, migration, and tissue geometry interact with genetic programs during a bounded morphogenetic event. Compare models with and without mechanical feedback.
strategies.summary: A falsifiable prediction of shape or tissue rearrangement.

strategies.title: Robustness, noise, and developmental correction
strategies.approach: Quantify how an embryo maintains reliable patterning despite variable gene expression, initial conditions, and localized disturbances. Compare feedback, redundancy, and self-organization mechanisms.
strategies.summary: A noise or perturbation tolerance curve with predicted recovery limits.

strategies.title: Predicting phenotypes from genetic changes
strategies.approach: Choose a tractable developmental system and test whether an integrated model predicts the effects of held-out genetic perturbations on cell types and anatomy. Assess uncertainty and transfer across environments.
